Things that make a man's
week feel twice as productive
Plan the week on Sunday in ten minutes. Three main goals, the key appointments, the training days. A week with a plan feels calm instead of chaotic.
Batch the boring tasks. Emails twice a day, errands on one afternoon, calls back to back. Grouping small jobs saves hours of switching between them.
Do the hardest thing before lunch. Your focus is strongest in the morning. Use it for the one task you'd otherwise keep pushing to tomorrow.
Say no to one meeting a week. Ask "Do you need me there, or can I read the notes?" Protected time is where your real work actually gets done.
Before: busy all week, little to show for it. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a clearer mind that knows what really matters.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: busy all week, little to show for it. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. Now my mind knows what really matters.

slides.texte_overlay: Move your body daily. A run, a walk, a short workout. Movement clears your head and gives you fresh energy for the second half of the day.
Review on Friday. Five minutes: what got done, what didn't, what to change. Small weekly reviews make every week a little better than the last.
